subject: Invoice delivery route & billing contact (portal vs email)
messages:
From: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@greenline.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-11T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Invoice delivery route & billing contact (portal vs email)

Hi Michael,

We're getting ready to onboard Redwood invoices into our AP workflow and a couple of items came up from our finance team. We want to confirm the recommended delivery path for invoices and where the billing contact should be set. Specifically: 

- We have two legal entities that will be billed depending on usage (Greenline AI Ltd. and Greenline AI US Inc.). Can Redwood emit separate invoices per entity, or do we need to split manually?
- We'd prefer to automate ingestion into our AP system. Is the Redwood portal the recommended path for that, or do you send structured e-invoice/XML over SFTP?
- If we stick with emailed PDFs, can you include a per-line VAT breakdown and the VAT registration number on each invoice?

Attached is our PO for the pilot month (PO_67421.pdf). Could you confirm next steps and who on your side should be the billing contact?

Thanks,
Sarah Cho
Director, Finance
Greenline AI

Attachment: PO_67421.pdf
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@greenline.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-11T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice delivery route & billing contact (portal vs email)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear note and the PO. Short answers up front: portal for AP automation is our recommended path; we can also emit per-entity invoices and include VAT line items. If you prefer emailed PDFs as a fallback we can do that too.

High-level options (we can implement any of these):
- Portal enrollment (recommended): Redwood will create a Greenline AP tenant. Invoices can be generated per legal-entity and pushed to your AP via SFTP or webhook/EDI connector. You can also enable \"Send copies to AP email\" so AP gets a PDF copy for human review.
- Email delivery: We will email a PDF to the billing contact. PDFs will include VAT breakdowns and VAT registration numbers. This is simpler but harder to automate reliably.

Next steps I need from you:
1) Confirm which of your two legal entities should receive which types of usage (or if we should split by billing tag).
2) Confirm AP ingestion preference: portal + webhook/SFTP or emailed PDFs.
3) Provide the VAT registration numbers and the remit-to info for the entity/entities.

I've attached a sample invoice template (sample-invoice-template.csv) so you can see field names we'll populate. Once we have the details Connor will scope the portal enrollment and Laura will run a quick compliance check for VAT evidence.

If portal is fine we can schedule enrollment this week and target first portal-issued invoice at the start of next billing cycle.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Lead, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sample-invoice-template.csv

Quick internal note on compliance and ops considerations before we confirm to the customer: 

1) VAT evidence: we need the VAT registration number for the EU entity and the US EIN for the US entity. For EU invoices we should include the VAT breakdown per line and the VAT total at the invoice footer. If Greenline expects reverse-charge handling, we need their confirmation and VAT place-of-supply.

2) Per-entity splitting: we can emit separate invoices per legal entity if they have distinct billing tags. Connor, please confirm whether that requires a separate billing account in the portal or if our back-end can map tags to invoice issuer.

3) Delivery options mapping: 
   - Portal + SFTP/webhook: best for automation and reconciliation. Portal can be set to produce one invoice per entity at month-end.
   - Email PDF: ok for immediate onboarding but we'll mark it as \"manual reconciliation\" in the account so AR knows to expect emailed remittances.

4) Attachments & PO matching: ask customer to include PO number in the portal enrollment form or as a billing tag; that will let us auto-match payments to invoices.

If customer chooses portal: we should offer a one-week onboarding window (config + test push) and then make the first live invoice at the start of their next billing cycle. If they choose email-only, we can send PDFs immediately but flag for a future portal enroll.

I'll take point on compliance review once Connor says whether per-entity requires account split.

Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations (Compliance)
Redwood Inference

Hi Michael / Laura / Connor —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We reviewed internally and want to move forward with the portal enrollment and SFTP delivery to our AP system. Confirmations below: 

- Billing entities: Greenline AI Ltd. (EU) will be billed for EU-region usage; Greenline AI US Inc. (US) for US-region usage. We will provide VAT/EIN numbers in the enrollment form.
- AP ingestion: portal -> SFTP is preferred. Please enable \"per-entity invoices\" and also set the portal to send a PDF copy to ap@greenline.ai for our records.
- PO matching: use PO_67421 for the pilot month and we'll include PO in the enrollment metadata going forward.
- VAT breakdown: yes, we require per-line VAT amounts and the VAT registration number on each invoice.

Can you confirm an expected enrollment window and the date the first portal-issued invoice will land? Also confirm the SFTP details and test file schedule so our AP team can stand up the import.

Thanks,
Sarah Cho
Director, Finance
Greenline AI
